prompt: Why does every tool command in this lesson start with `docker run --rm`?
hint: What would a hundred runs leave behind?

choices.text: It removes the container when the command ends
choices.why: Right; otherwise each run leaves a stopped container.

choices.text: It runs the tool as root
choices.why: `--rm` says nothing about the user; `--user` does.

choices.text: It makes the container start faster by skipping the image's layers entirely
choices.why: Layers are always used; `--rm` only affects what happens after the end.

choices.text: It mounts the current directory
choices.why: That is `-v "$PWD":/work`.

prompt: In `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work mikefarah/yq:4 ".database.port" config.yaml`, what does `-w /work` do?

choices.text: Makes `/work` writable
choices.why: The mount is writable by default; `-w` is about where the command starts.

choices.text: Sets the working directory
choices.why: Right: the command starts in `/work`, so `config.yaml` is found by its relative name.

choices.text: Waits for `/work` to be ready
choices.why: There is nothing to wait for; it sets a directory.

choices.text: Watches `/work` for changes
choices.why: No watching; the command runs once.

prompt: Hadolint read Ana's Dockerfile with nothing mounted. How?
hint: Look at the end of the command.

choices.text: Docker copied the current directory into the container
choices.why: Nothing is copied into a container unless mounted or built in.

choices.text: Hadolint downloads the file from Ana's repository
choices.why: It has no idea where the repository is.

choices.text: Piped to stdin, kept open by `-i`
choices.why: Right: `< Dockerfile` and `-`, read from stdin.

choices.text: Hadolint is installed on the host after all
choices.why: `which` found no hadolint.

prompt: What could happen with `tar -czf $target/backup.tar.gz /srv/data` if `target` is `/mnt/my disk`?
hint: What does the shell do with an unquoted variable?

choices.text: Nothing different; `tar` handles spaces in paths on its own
choices.why: `tar` never sees one argument; the shell has already split it.

choices.text: ShellCheck fixes the script when it runs
choices.why: It reports; it changes no file.

choices.text: The backup is encrypted
choices.why: Quoting has nothing to do with encryption.

choices.text: The shell splits it, and `tar` writes elsewhere
choices.why: Right: SC2086. Quote it, as ShellCheck suggested.

pairs.right: `apt-get install` would stop to ask a question
The package lists stay inside the image

right_distractors: The image is too large to push

prompt: `stats.py` printed a `Loan` under `python:3.13-slim` and an `AttributeError` under `python:3.12-slim`. Why?

choices.text: `copy.replace` does not exist before Python 3.13
choices.why: Right. The tag decided which Python ran the file.

choices.text: The 3.12 image is broken
choices.why: It ran Python fine; the function is missing from that version.

choices.text: Slim images remove the `copy` module
choices.why: Both are slim, and `copy` imported in both.

choices.text: The file was mounted read-only for 3.12
choices.why: Both runs used the same mount, and reading worked.

prompt: So that files a containerised tool writes into your directory belong to you, run it with `--___ "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`.
hint: One word: whose identity the process takes.

prompt: In the wrapper, why `"$@"` and not `$*`?
hint: What happens to an argument that contains a space?

choices.text: `$*` is not valid inside a function body in bash
choices.why: It is valid; it just joins and re-splits the arguments.

choices.text: Each argument stays intact, spaces and all
choices.why: Right. `$*` would re-split `".x | length"` into pieces.

choices.text: `"$@"` is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the difference.

choices.text: `$*` would also pass the image name along to yq
choices.why: Neither includes anything but the function's own arguments.

prompt: Ana's function uses `mikefarah/yq:4`. What does writing the tag do for her?
hint: What would happen with no tag at all?

choices.text: Downloads version 4 on every call
choices.why: Once pulled, the image is reused until she pulls again.

choices.text: Makes yq run four times faster
choices.why: The number is a version, not a speed.

choices.text: Keeps yq on major version 4
choices.why: Right. Without a tag she would get `latest`, whatever that is that day.

choices.text: Limits the container to four processes
choices.why: That would be `--pids-limit`, from lesson 4.

prompt: `yq ".x" ../other.yaml` says "no such file or directory", yet the file exists one directory up. Why?

choices.text: yq cannot read files whose names end in `.yaml`
choices.why: It read `config.yaml` a moment before.

choices.text: The file is owned by root
choices.why: Ana created it as herself; ownership is not the issue.

choices.text: Docker hides files starting with `..`
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; the parent directory simply is not there.

choices.text: Only the current directory was mounted
choices.why: Right: the path leaves the container's files; inside, `../other.yaml` is `/other.yaml`.

prompt: How many seconds of wall-clock time did `time yq --version` report? Use the `real` value.
hint: The first of the three lines.

prompt: Mounting `~/.aws` read-only into an image makes the AWS tool work. What does it also do?
hint: Who can read what is mounted?

choices.text: Hands the credentials to whatever program is in that image
choices.why: Right, so the image's origin matters; lesson 20.

choices.text: Makes the credentials expire
choices.why: Nothing about mounting changes the credentials.

choices.text: Uploads them to Docker Hub
choices.why: A mount stays on the machine.

choices.text: Nothing more, because `:ro` keeps the credentials safe from the image
choices.why: `:ro` stops writing, not reading.

prompt: Which of these does a containerised command-line tool NOT see unless you arrange it? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Files outside the mounted directory
choices.why: Yes: only what is mounted exists inside.

choices.text: Services on the host's `localhost`
choices.why: Yes: inside a container, `localhost` is the container. Lesson 23.

choices.text: The arguments typed after the image name
choices.why: Those are handed to the entrypoint every time.

choices.text: A graphical display
choices.why: Yes: a container has none without extra work.

prompt: Why do CI pipelines run linters and scanners as `docker run` of a pinned image?
hint: What does the runner need installed?

choices.text: Docker images run linters faster than native installs
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; a container adds start-up time.

choices.text: Only Docker, and the same line gives the same answer on a laptop
choices.why: Right. The tool's version travels in the tag.

choices.text: Linters refuse to run outside containers
choices.why: They run fine natively; the point is not having to install them.

choices.text: It hides the source code from the linter
choices.why: The code is mounted precisely so the linter can read it.

prompt: A script calls the `yq` wrapper once for each of 2,000 YAML files. What is the main cost, and the fix?

choices.text: Disk space for 2,000 images; prune afterwards
choices.why: One image is reused; no new images are made.

choices.text: Network traffic to Docker Hub; use a mirror
choices.why: The image is local after the first pull.

choices.text: 2,000 container start-ups; give yq all the files in one run, or install it
choices.why: Right: about a third of a second each.

choices.text: Memory; add `--memory`
choices.why: Each container is short and small; the start-up time is what adds up.
